newsitem.title: MEXICO: Penoles digging for new mining investments.
newsitem.headline: Penoles digging for new mining investments.

text.p: The world's largest silver producer, Mexico's Penoles SA, said on Tuesday it is on the lookout for investment opportunities with ready cash left over from an aborted Peruvian mine purchase.

Company officials said they have cash from a recent $380 million silver-backed loan to explore joint ventures or possible projects in Chile and Venezuela, according to analysts who participated in a conference call with the company.
"Potential acquisitions and joint ventures currently being considered (amount to) $365 million," Penoles said in a statement obtained by Reuters on Tuesday.

But analysts agreed that Penoles would be wary of returning to Peru, where the company had agreed to buy the La Oroya mine from mining company Centromin, yet cut out in a surprise move earlier this month.

"It doesn't make sense for Penoles to go back to Peru. They say they still have a good relationship (with Centromin) but there must be a little bit of bad blood between them because of what's happened," London Paribas analyst Nigel Kieser said.
During the conference call, Penoles officials lashed back against recent Centromin jabs at the Mexican silver giant.
Officials at the company said they were not given full access to the mine until after they purchased it, and were not offered enough for the transfer of its technology.

"Obviously they (Centromin) decided to lump more liabilities on Penoles after they sold the thing, which does not set a good precedent for remaining Peruvian auctions in the mining sphere," Kieser said.
Merrill Lynch's Rene Kleyweg said the company has a cash balance of about $500 million and a healthy cash flow compared to other metals companies.
"The message they are sending is they have money to invest...but they will be selective," he said.
Kleyweg added that in a worst case scenario the company would leave the amount in cash and pay back its debt with the balance.
Penoles said in the statement that it spent a total 339.5 million pesos on investments in the first six months at its La Herradura gold mine and its Met-Mex zinc plant, among others.
Further investments on projects through 1999 are expecte to total $644 million, the company said.
